en.name: Lima beans
en.summary: Lima beans are large flat beans sold in the pod or already shelled, starchy and buttery when cooked. In the pod they keep 3–5 days in the fridge from the day of purchase, and blanched and frozen they hold good quality for about 8 months.
en.pantry: Lima beans should not be kept at room temperature. Fresh beans are respiring hard, turning sugar to starch and losing their sweetness within a day in a warm kitchen, and shelled beans dry out and discolour even faster. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate them in the pod the moment you get home.
en.fridge: Keep lima beans in their pods, unwashed, in a perforated bag in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where they last 3–5 days from purchase. The pod holds moisture in and keeps the skins tender, so it is worth the space. Beans you have already shelled go faster — cover them and use them within a day. Never eat lima beans raw: they contain cyanogenic compounds and must be cooked, uncovered, in plenty of water.
en.freezer: Lima beans freeze well and are one of the classic freezer vegetables. Shell them, boil for 2–3 minutes, plunge into iced water, drain thoroughly and pack airtight at −18 °C (0 °F). They are safe indefinitely and keep good quality for about 8 months. Freeze them blanched rather than raw; the blanching also counts towards the cooking they need.
en.thawing: Add frozen lima beans straight to soups, stews and braises without thawing, and cook them through — they need proper boiling, not just reheating. Do not thaw them slowly on the counter.
spoilage: Pods gone brown, blackened or leathery
Beans inside shrivelled, spotted or discoloured
Slimy or mouldy patches, especially at the stem end
A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened
tips: Buy pods that feel full and give slightly when squeezed; flat pods are mostly waste.
Shell them only when you are ready to cook.
Boil lima beans uncovered in plenty of water; never eat them raw or undercooked.
Expect roughly a third of the pod weight to end up as beans.

faq.q: How long do fresh lima beans last in the fridge?
faq.a: 3–5 days from the day of purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept in the pod in a perforated bag.
Yes. Shell, blanch for 2–3 minutes, chill and pack airtight at −18 °C (0 °F) for about 8 months of good quality.

faq.q: Can you eat lima beans raw?
faq.a: No. They contain cyanogenic compounds and must be cooked thoroughly. Boil them in plenty of water with the lid off.

faq.q: Why did my lima beans go grey?
faq.a: Usually overcooking or long storage after shelling. Grey beans that smell clean are safe if cooked, but the texture and flavour will have suffered.

zh.name: 皇帝豆
zh.summary: 皇帝豆是連莢或已剝好販售的大型扁豆，煮熟後口感鬆軟帶奶香。連莢冷藏從購買當天算起可放 3～5 天；汆燙後冷凍則可維持約 8 個月的良好品質。
zh.pantry: 皇帝豆不應該放室溫。新鮮豆子呼吸旺盛，會把糖轉成澱粉，在溫暖的廚房裡一天甜味就流失；已經剝好的豆仁更是乾得快、也更快變色。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請連莢立刻冷藏。
zh.fridge: 請連莢、不清洗，裝進打洞袋放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，從購買日起可放 3～5 天。豆莢能鎖住水分、也讓豆皮保持柔軟，值得佔那點空間。已經剝好的豆仁壞得更快——請蓋好並在隔天用完。皇帝豆絕對不能生吃：它含有氰苷類成分，必須開蓋用足量的水徹底煮熟。
zh.freezer: 皇帝豆很適合冷凍，是經典的冷凍蔬菜之一。剝出豆仁，滾水煮 2～3 分鐘，泡冰水冷卻，徹底瀝乾後密封放 −18°C。安全上可無限期保存，品質可維持約 8 個月。請汆燙後再冷凍而不是生凍；汆燙也算是它所需要的加熱的一部分。
zh.thawing: 冷凍皇帝豆請不解凍直接下湯、下燉鍋，並確實煮熟——它需要真正的滾煮，不是加熱一下就好。不要放在室溫慢慢解凍。
spoilage: 豆莢轉褐、發黑或變得像皮革
裡面的豆仁皺縮、長斑或變色
出現黏滑或發霉的區塊，尤其是蒂頭附近
打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味
tips: 挑豆莢飽滿、輕捏會略有彈性的；扁扁的莢幾乎都是廢料。
用足量的水、開著蓋煮；絕對不要生吃或半生食用。
豆莢重量大約只有三分之一會變成豆仁，份量要抓夠。

faq.q: 新鮮皇帝豆放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、連莢裝在打洞袋裡，從購買當天算起 3～5 天。
可以。剝出豆仁、汆燙 2～3 分鐘、冰鎮後密封放 −18°C，品質可維持約 8 個月。
不行。它含有氰苷類成分，必須徹底煮熟，請開著蓋用足量的水煮。
多半是煮過頭，或是剝好後放太久。只要氣味乾淨、確實煮熟就仍可食用，但口感和風味都已經打折。
